description: Concurrent use significantly increases the risk of bleeding, including gastrointestinal and intracranial hemorrhage. Avoid combination unless benefit clearly outweighs risk; monitor INR closely if co-administered.
Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism, raising INR and bleeding risk. Reduce warfarin dose by roughly one-third to one-half when starting amiodarone and monitor INR frequently.
ACE inhibitors reduce potassium excretion; combining with potassium supplements can cause hyperkalemia. Monitor serum potassium periodically.

Iodinated contrast can impair renal function, increasing the risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis. Hold metformin before and for 48 hours after contrast administration in patients with reduced renal function.
Clarithromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of simvastatin, raising myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk. Avoid combination; suspend simvastatin during clarithromycin therapy.
Combination increases serotonin syndrome risk due to additive serotonergic effects. Use only with caution and close monitoring for agitation, hyperthermia, and clonus.
Both agents raise serum potassium; combined use increases hyperkalemia risk, particularly with renal impairment. Monitor potassium and renal function.
Furosemide-induced hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity. Monitor serum potassium and digoxin levels, particularly after diuretic dose changes.
